brief: JPM Market Intelligence morning briefing. Rates and oil are treated as effectively one trade. There is no real progress on US vs Iran, but a record 18m barrels moving through the Strait of Hormuz points at reduced ability to disrupt flows, which the author reads as welcome for Europe, where gas reserves are low and the Street cites risk of TTF at 100 euros a megawatt-hour before year-end. Gold bounced at its 100-day moving average on speculation of fresh Japanese intervention. Whether that is the bottom depends on a September Fed hike, but the author still expects the trend to resume before year-end. AI value-chain data has accelerated since June while de-rating continued, so hedge fund performance stayed choppy in August. Seasonal re-grossing could support alpha spreads going forward. Positioning is back to neutral in most regions after August de-grossing flipped to re-grossing late in the month, and momentum was sold back to year-to-date lows. The desk is tactically cautious or neutral on global equities, prefers US and Asia over Europe, is high conviction short EU Chemicals and Asia Consumer Electronics, and is bullish EM expressed through country-relative trades.
